definition: Task can be done to standard with no presence in the place and no field-formed expertise.
rater_anchor_example: Reconcile a budget spreadsheet; draft a public notice.
notes: Weights 0/1/2 per craft; the three are rated independently (they need not sum to anything).

definition: Supporting: field presence or field-formed expertise improves the result or catches errors, but a practitioner without it can still meet intermediate standard.
rater_anchor_example: Fit a growth model to inventory data (field knowledge catches implausible parameters).
notes: v1 "FC-secondary" maps here by default during migration.

definition: Defining: the task fails without one of the field components - direct perception of the site, measurement integrity at the point of observation, situated action or intervention, physical-operational skill, or risk management in an uncontrolled environment.
rater_anchor_example: Estimate soil texture by feel; fell a tree; hold line on a prescribed burn; calibrate a sonde in the stream; verify a burn-severity polygon on the ground.
notes: v1 "FC-primary" maps to 2 for tasks that pass the presence or ground-truth test; re-rate others.

definition: As above for data craft: 2 = the task fails without structuring, analysing, modelling or validating information beyond what direct observation gives.
rater_anchor_example: 2: build an occupancy model; 1: design a field data form; 0: hand-fell a snag.
notes: DC lead owns the anchor wording; listed here so FC raters use the same scale.

definition: As above for statecraft: 2 = the task fails without institutional authority, legal process, negotiation or relationships across institutions.
rater_anchor_example: 2: negotiate a grazing permit modification; 1: brief a landowner on survey findings; 0: measure stream discharge.
notes: SC lead owns the anchor wording.

definition: Task must be performed in the place, at the time (physical action, sampling, in-person inspection, real-time field decisions).
rater_anchor_example: Collect water samples; burn boss go/no-go; fireline construction.
notes: Not a craft weight. Drives duty station, fitness, safety training, telework and travel planning.

definition: Usually done on site but can be partly done remotely with tools (e.g., remote piloting from a nearby base, remote review of sensor feeds with periodic visits).
rater_anchor_example: Drone survey from a launch point; sensor network servicing with telemetry checks.

definition: Can be done fully off site, though field visits sometimes improve it.
rater_anchor_example: Review AI-flagged camera-trap images; plan a field season.

definition: Competent performance requires expertise formed through supervised field exposure, even if the task itself is done remotely.
rater_anchor_example: Adjudicating AI species identifications; ground-truth sample design; reviewing a burn plan.
notes: Replaces v1 rule "assign FC-secondary liberally". Flags where curricula and hiring must keep field formation even for desk roles.

definition: The expertise can be built entirely through study, desk practice or simulation.
The field skill transfers across ecosystems and regions with brief orientation.
notes: Feeds mobility: general field skill is portable across sector actors and regions.

definition: Transfers within an ecosystem type or region (flora, soils, fire regimes) but needs re-learning elsewhere.
rater_anchor_example: Regional plant identification; fire behavior in a fuel type.
notes: Mobility across regions carries a re-learning cost; across sector actors in the same region it does not.

definition: Knowledge of a particular place, its history and variability, accumulated over time there.
rater_anchor_example: Knowing where a creek floods first; history of a grazing allotment.
notes: Most at risk when long-tenure staff leave; recognize, do not codify (see report Section 7).

definition: How many natural cycles a learner must experience to see the range of conditions: none; one or more seasons; multi-year or rare events (floods, escapes, outbreaks).
rater_anchor_example: Rare-event: escaped prescribed fire response; seasonal: phenology-dependent plant ID.
notes: Rare-event skills need simulation, sand tables or exercises because field exposure cannot be scheduled.

definition: How much supervised, in-place practice with an experienced practitioner competent performance requires.
rater_anchor_example: High: felling, burn boss, wetland delineation; low: running a standard meter.

definition: Whether performance is gated by a qualification (e.g., NWCG position), an external certificate (e.g., Part 107, HAZWOPER, pesticide applicator) or a license.
rater_anchor_example: Internal: sawyer certification; external: Part 107; license: pesticide applicator.
notes: Credentials live in the credential/tool layer and link to tasks; they are inputs, not proficiency evidence.

definition: How fast proficiency decays without practice (drives currency requirements and refreshers).
rater_anchor_example: High: aerial ignition, saw felling, wilderness medicine; low: soil description.
